Question: If \(m\) and \(b\) are real numbers and \(mb\gt0,\) then the line whose equation is \(y=mx+b\) cannot contain the point
Solution:
The condition \(mb>0\) says that \(m\) and \(b\) are nonzero and have the same sign. At the horizontal intercept, \(y=0\), so
\[
0=mx+b,
\qquad x=-\frac bm<0.
\]
Division by \(m\) is valid because \(m\ne0\). Thus every allowed line crosses the horizontal axis at a negative coordinate, making \((1997,0)\) impossible.

The other options really are possible. The lines
\[
\begin{aligned}
y&=x+1997,\\
y&=-x-1997,\\
y&=x+78,\\
y&=-x-78
\end{aligned}
\]
contain the points in choices A, B, C, and D, respectively, and each has \(mb>0\). Therefore the excluded point is \(\boxed{(1997,0)}\), choice \(\mathrm E\).
